newsitem.title: UK: Astra launches Naropin anaesthetic in UK.
newsitem.headline: Astra launches Naropin anaesthetic in UK.

text.p: Swedish drug giant Astra AB launched its local anaesthetic Naropin in Britain on Thursday, hailing the product as a major advance in easing childbirth.
The company said Naropin, available next week to British hospitals, blocks pain at low doses with less effect on mobility than other local anaesthetics.
The drug achieves this by targeting the sensory nerves, which control pain, more than the motor nerves, which control muscle, leaving women more mobile during labour.
"I'm personally delighted with this," John McClure, a consultant anaesthetist at Edinburgh Royal Infirmary, told a news conference to launch the drug.
"If the mother is able to move about and participate more fully in the birth, this can greatly improve maternal satisfaction," he said.

Astra said Naropin could also be used at higher doses to provide motor and sensory block, making it an ideal local anaesthetic for orthopaedic surgery, hysterectomies, bladder surgery and Caesarean sections.
The company estimated the cash value of the market in Britain for another anaesthetic used in childbirth, bupivacaine, at about 4.0 million stg per year.
Naropin, which has been approved in some 15 countries, has already been launched in the U.S., Australia, Sweden, Finland, Denmark, and the Netherlands, a company official said.
He declined to give sales targets for the product.
